patch.value: Starting work ignores open blockers: claim <id> --start and update --status in_progress move a blocked item into progress without a refusal or warning

Raised by CodeRabbit on PR #1645 and verified on 2026.10.31 source in a fresh sandbox. An item created with --blocked-by <open item> is stored as status blocked, and pm update <id> --status in_progress then succeeds with no refusal or warning. pm claim <id> --start runs the same claim-then-update composition, so it behaves the same. pm validate later reports non_blocked_status_has_blocked_by for the in-progress item whose blocker is still open. pm next and claim --next --start are unaffected because ready selection already excludes items with open blockers. Starting an explicitly blocked item is a governance decision, not a claim defect, so changing only --start would make start and update disagree.

Duplicate search: 'start blocked item open blocker in_progress refuse', 'non_blocked_status_has_blocked_by' — no open item. Nearest is the dependency-aware actionability decision (closed).

Moving an item with an open blocked_by target into the in-progress status, through update, claim --start or start-task, either refuses with a typed code naming the open blocker and the unblock or --force recovery, or warns, as governed by a declared setting; the CLI, MCP and SDK paths share one check that runs before any write, so a refused start never leaves a claim; a terminal blocker does not block; tests cover refuse, warn and terminal-blocker cases
No transport can silently move an item with an open blocker into progress; the behaviour is declared by governance settings and consistent across update and start.
